Each face gets 100 N. The defined force is applied uniformly to the selected objects, so a 200 N force load on two faces of equal area loads each face uniformly with 100 N.
The FreeCAD FEM ConstraintForce uses the *CLOAD card in CalculiX.

FreeCAD uses Gmsh as the default mesher to create a FEM Mesh. Depending on your OS and installation, Gmsh may be bundled with FreeCAD; if not, install it separately and set its path in Edit → Preferences → FEM → Gmsh.
Install Gmsh separately, then use the menu Edit → Preferences → FEM → Gmsh to set the path to the gmsh.exe.

Try these strategies: 1) Set Data Second Order Linear to true but keep Data Element Order at 2nd. 2) Set Data Element Order to 1st. 3) Use a smaller element size by reducing Data Characteristic Length Max. If solver ccxtools is used and the run button is used (not the task panel), the nodes of nonpositive jacobian elements will be green.
Elmer does not support Netgen meshes.

Run the single command ccx in the terminal. If CalculiX is correctly installed, you get a simple response: "Usage: CalculiX.exe -i jobname". Then make sure the FEM Workbench can find the binary via Edit → Preferences → FEM → CalculiX → Search in known binary directories. If you compiled the solver yourself, untick that option and give the correct path to the binary.

The original framework Solver CalculiX Standard is preferred because it contains extra checks, e.g. showing the elements with nonpositive Jacobian, which might cause solution difficulties. The new-framework solver uses the same framework as the Elmer and Z88 solvers, and its code is not visible to the user.

In FreeCAD 0.21 and below, the FEM ConstraintSelfWeight uses a fixed gravity acceleration of 9.81 m/s^2 (9810 mm/s^2 in the CalculiX .inp file). It can only be changed by manually editing the .inp file.
If checked, multiple *.inp files are written and the main input deck uses the *INCLUDE keywords to reference the other ones. If unchecked, a single large *.inp file is written.
The PartDesign Pad tool extrudes a sketch or a face along a straight path. It is found under Part Design → Additive Features → Pad.
A positive taper angle tapers the pad in the extrusion direction so that the outer pad border gets wider. The option is only available if Type is Dimension.
For technical reasons, a Through All pocket is actually 10 meters deep. It extends up to the last face of the support it encounters in its direction. For deeper pockets, use the type Dimension.

The Tip is the PartDesign Feature that is exposed outside the Body; other tools from any workbench (e.g. Part SimpleCopy or Part Cut) use the shape of the Tip, so it is the final representation of the Body as if the parametric history didn't exist. By default, the Tip is automatically set to the last feature created in the Body (it can be changed via Set Tip in the Tree View context menu or the Body's Data Tip property).
The Hole feature can create countersink, counterbore, and straight holes. Parameters such as threading, size and fit can also be set.

Edge numbers are not completely stable. If you apply fillets and chamfers before finishing the main design, edges could change names (the topological naming problem) and the filleted edges would likely become invalid. Setting Data Use All Edges to true gives some protection, because all edges of the base object are used and nothing depends on individual edge names.

Differences from the Part Extrude documentation:
- Part Extrude always creates a standalone shape; PartDesign Pad fuses the extrusion result to the rest of the Body.
- Part Extrude can be placed anywhere in the model tree; PartDesign Pad can only be placed inside a PartDesign Body.
- Part Extrude can extrude any object with a Part geometry (OpenCASCADE shape) except solids and CompSolids; it can also extrude individual faces of other objects.
- PartDesign Pad only accepts a Sketch or faces of PartDesign objects as a profile.

Boolean operations are done by the OpenCASCADE Technology (OCCT) geometry kernel, which sometimes has problems producing results when the input objects share an edge or a face (coplanarity). A cut or union of shapes sharing a face may give incorrect results. Even if the first boolean succeeds, later ones may fail, and the real problem may be in older, nested operations shown in the Tree View. Recommended: make the shapes intersect clearly (one protrudes or is larger than the other) and use Part CheckGeometry to inspect objects for problems.

The Sketcher ConstrainLock (Lock Position) tool applies a horizontal dimension constraint and a vertical dimension constraint to a point. With a single point selected, they reference the sketch origin; with two or more points selected, they reference the last point in the selection.
An unconstrained line in the Sketcher has 4 degrees of freedom (DoF): it can be moved horizontally or vertically, stretched, and rotated.
If two lines are selected (or a line and the endpoint of another line), the Sketcher ConstrainTangent tool makes the lines collinear instead of tangent.
FreeCAD macros are single files of Python code ending with the .FCMacro extension.

Run the installer from the command line with the /S flag: FreeCAD-~.exe /S. Default settings are used for all options. To use a custom installation path, add /D: FreeCAD-~.exe /S /D=A path to FreeCAD with spaces. Even in silent mode a short popup appears while the installer is checked for corruption (a cyclic redundancy check). You can disable it with /NCRC (FreeCAD-~.exe /S /NCRC), but this is not recommended because the check confirms the installer was completely downloaded.

With HomeBrew installed, run in your terminal: `brew install --cask freecad`. To use the latest version available on HomeBrew, run `brew install freecad`. Issues with the HomeBrew Cask or Formula can be reported to the maintainers.

The Assembly Workbench uses the open-source Ondsel solver.
FreeCAD expressions support two constants: e (Euler's number) and pi (Pi).

Each FreeCAD object has a Data Placement property, which contains the Data Base (position) and Data Rotation (orientation) of the object. In scripting it is accessed as e.g. box.Placement, with box.Placement.Base holding the position vector, and it can be replaced with a FreeCAD.Placement() object. The excerpts do not describe any lower-level internal storage beyond this.
The Std Measure command gives access to the Unified Measurement Facility. It replaces several previous measurement commands and provides versatile measurement functionality.

For structures, *BOUNDARY prescribes temperature, displacements and rotations. The degrees of freedom are: 1-3 translation in the local x, y, z direction; 4-6 rotation about the local x, y, z axis (only for nodes belonging to beams or shells); and 11 temperature.
Degree of freedom 11 represents temperature in the *BOUNDARY card (for structures, and also 11 for temperature in gas/liquid networks and channels, where it is total temperature for gas networks).

Use the *CLOAD keyword card. In the cantilever beam example, a concentrated load is applied with *CLOAD to the node set LOAD, with forces acting in y-direction and magnitude 1 per node. The format is node (or node set), direction, magnitude, e.g. *CLOAD 4000,1,10 applies a point force of 10 in direction 1 to node 4000 (the reference node of a distributing coupling). *CLOAD is placed inside a *STEP, e.g. after the *STATIC procedure card.

According to the *DENSITY keyword description, the mass density is required for a frequency analysis (*FREQUENCY), for a dynamic analysis (*DYNAMIC or *HEAT TRANSFER), and for a static analysis with gravity loads (GRAV) or centrifugal loads (CENTRIF). It can be temperature dependent.

A material name given in the NAME parameter of *MATERIAL can contain up to 80 characters. Some special material types restrict this: for example, a single crystal material name has to start with "SINGLE CRYSTAL" but can still be up to 80 characters long.

Use the *FREQUENCY step card and enter the number of eigenfrequencies desired on the second line. For example, `*FREQUENCY` followed by `10` requests the calculation of the 10 lowest eigenfrequencies and corresponding eigenmodes. Optionally, the lower and upper bounds of the frequency range can also be given on that line (lower default: 0). If you also want Coriolis effects, a *COMPLEX FREQUENCY,CORIOLIS step with 10 can follow a *FREQUENCY step that uses STORAGE=YES.

C3D10 is a 10-node quadratic tetrahedral element. It is a general purpose tetrahedral element with 4 integration points, and the manual says it behaves very well. It is attractive because fully automatic tetrahedral meshers exist for it, although C3D20R yields still better results for the same number of degrees of freedom.

For *STATIC, the SOLVER default is the first installed solver from this list: SGI, PaStiX, PARDISO, SPOOLES and TAUCS. If none is installed, the default is the iterative solver that comes with the CalculiX package.

No special compilation flag is needed. At execution time set the environment variable OMP NUM THREADS or CCX NPROC STIFFNESS to the number of cores (default is 1). If both are set, CCX NPROC STIFFNESS takes precedence. CalculiX detects the maximum number of cores automatically with sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF), which you can override with the environment variable NUMBER OF CPUS.

CalculiX has no built-in units: finite element programs do not know any units, so the user must provide numbers with consistent units. For thermomechanical problems you can freely choose four units (e.g. length, mass, time, temperature), and all others follow. Examples: SI (m, kg, s, K) gives force in N and steel density 7800 kg/m3; (mm, g, s, K) gives steel density 7.8e-6 g/mm3 and force in g·mm/s2; another common system is mm, N, s, K. Table 1 compares the m,kg,s,K, mm,N,s,K and cm,g,s,K systems.

Run a linearized version first. Eliminate large deformations (drop NLGEOM), use a linear elastic material, and drop all other nonlinearities such as contact. If the linear version doesn't run, the nonlinear problem won't run either. The linear run also lets you check that the boundary conditions are correct (no unrestrained rigid body modes) and that the loading is the one you meant to apply, and it gives you a feeling for what the solution should look like.
The parameters ELSET and MATERIAL are required on the *SOLID SECTION card. ORIENTATION and NODAL THICKNESS are optional.
Every *STEP card must at some point be followed by an *END STEP card, which concludes the step definition.

*BUCKLE performs a buckling calculation: it solves an iterative eigenvalue problem to find the buckling load, i.e. the requested number of buckling factors (usually 1). For example, *BUCKLE with 2 on the second line computes the lowest two buckling modes and their buckling factors. The eigenvalues are automatically stored in jobname.dat.
